assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and changed what can be measured: relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants, searches for dark matter and a path to redefining the second. Few advances in precision measurement have so directly extended the reach of experiment.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first Sr lattice clock; Ye drove the systematic accuracy and stability records and the many-body (Fermi-degenerate) clock. A two-person prize is clean and fits the supplied credit. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Ludlow and others, not on the list) contributed, so some credit is left out.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs now operate lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level and intercompare them, so confirmation is strong. Timing is good given the redefinition discussions and the earlier Hall/Hänsch and Wineland recognition of the underlying toolbox.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion control may be argued against novelty.
I have not independently verified the latest uncertainty records and the Sr-versus-Yb priority details.
Whether the committee prefers to include a third name for the clock-comparison work is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single spins in NV centres and related defects, from Wrachtrup's single-molecule and single-NV work to Awschalom's coherent control in SiC and diamond and Lukin's nanoscale sensing and quantum registers, created a robust room-temperature quantum sensor and a solid-state qubit platform. Nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and in-cell sensing are real measurement advances.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup (first optical detection of a single NV spin), Awschalom (defect spin coherence, SiC and diamond) and Lukin (nanoscale sensing and registers) are a defensible trio. Walsworth, who is also credited, made key ensemble magnetometry and imaging contributions, so omitting him leaves an allocation question, and the fourth name cannot be included.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across many groups and already commercialised in sensing. The field is still evolving rapidly, but the central discoveries are over two decades old and stable.
uncertainties: Who first showed single NV spin detection and coherent control (Gruber et al. 1997, Jelezko et al. 2004) versus later sensing is a credit question.
Hard to draw a single discovery from a broad field with four credited names.
Impact on medicine and industry is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and the experimental realisation by Blatt and others turned a theoretical idea into controlled multi-qubit quantum processors with high-fidelity gates. This is a landmark in experimental quantum information and in the control of single quantum systems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theory proposal; Blatt led the most prominent demonstration of the gate and entanglement of several ions. Wineland and Monroe (not on the list) are central to the experimental side, and Wineland already has the 2012 prize, which complicates the story and the attribution of experimental credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation in several laboratories and in commercial devices. Timing is reasonable, though the 2012 and 2025 quantum-technology prizes may reduce the appetite for another quantum-control prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion control may weaken the case.
B019 appears to be the same triple with a broader label; I judged B031 to be the sharper discovery.
Whether the proposal or the experiments should dominate the credit is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the Ekert protocol founded quantum cryptography, with security guaranteed by physical principles, and experimental QKD from fibre to satellite has made it a measurable and tested technology. It is a clear example of quantum foundations turned into practice.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) and Ekert (E91) are the conceptual originators. Jian-Wei Pan led the satellite and long-distance experiments, which could be a separate, experimental recognition and cannot sensibly be combined with the three theory names in one prize.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are decades old and experimentally verified, but practical security, side channels and the real-world role of QKD relative to post-quantum cryptography remain debated.
uncertainties: Compound candidate: theory founders and experimental network builders may need separate recognition.
Real-world impact is contested and device security loopholes persist.
Overlap with Bell-test prize of 2022 on entanglement foundations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reached strong coupling of a superconducting qubit to a single microwave photon, enabling dispersive readout, quantum non-demolition measurement and the standard architecture of superconducting processors. It is both a measurement method and a platform with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the architecture with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf; Wallraff and Schoelkopf did the key experiments. The supplied trio is workable, though Girvin and Huang are missing from the credit and the 2025 prize to Clarke, Devoret and Martinis already covers parts of the field.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended by dozens of groups and underpinning present-day devices. Timeliness is good for the field but the 2025 prize may crowd out a close successor.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
Missing names in the supplied credit leave the allocation partly unresolved.
Whether the committee sees this as a method or as the platform achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers produce femtosecond, coherent, extremely bright pulses and opened time-resolved structural measurements on atoms, molecules and materials. As an instrument that extends what can be measured, it has had a very large effect on the physics, chemistry and biology it serves.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Kim and Rossbach are the key theorists and designers of SASE operation, but LCLS and European XFEL involved large teams and other accelerator physicists (e.g. Madey for the FEL concept, not on the list) are central. A fair prize configuration is possible but contentious.
assessment.maturity: Facilities operate worldwide with strong independent confirmation, and the science output is large. Recognition is timely, though the instrument-versus-physics balance and the earlier FEL history complicate it.
uncertainties: Credit for the original FEL concept and for the SASE idea is divided among many people.
Large collaborative facility effort is hard to reduce to three names.
Impact is largest in structural biology and chemistry, which may be seen as outside physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing arrays have given evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries and possibly early-universe physics. It is a remarkable long-baseline precision timing measurement.
assessment.attribution: The result comes from several large collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA) and the supplied three names represent only part of this effort; the decisive individuals are hard to isolate.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is roughly 3-4 sigma and the interpretation (astrophysical versus cosmological) is not settled, so recognition is likely premature until a definitive detection and individual source identification.
uncertainties: Statistical significance below the conventional discovery threshold in some analyses.
Source of the signal is not established.
Collaboration credit is diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire lasers, Kerr-lens modelocking and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors (SESAMs) made reliable solid-state femtosecond sources and enabled ultrafast spectroscopy, frequency combs and attosecond science. It is a technology that opened up measurement in time, and a favourite of mine for practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed the Ti:sapphire gain medium, Sibbett and colleagues demonstrated Kerr-lens modelocking, and Keller invented SESAMs and brought them to high-power use. The three contributions are distinct and a fair trio exists, but the Kerr-lens priority is debated.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous, with strong confirmation. Because earlier prizes (2005 combs, 2018 CPA, 2023 attosecond pulses) built on or around this technology, the incremental novelty relative to those awards is a concern.
uncertainties: Overlap with already awarded laser and ultrafast prizes.
Priority for Kerr-lens modelocking among Sibbett's group and others is not something I have verified.
Device invention rather than a physical discovery may weigh against it.
